column1: # Encoding, hashes and IDs functions. One row per function, per task it belongs to. Tab-separated; see finder.py for the rules.

column7: summary
Returns bytes or a string as base64 text, in the standard or URL-safe alphabet.
Decodes base64 text into a byte array and returns the byte count, or an error.
Decodes base64 text straight to a string; the decoded bytes must be UTF-8.
Returns bytes or a string as base32 text, in the standard or sortable hex alphabet.
Decodes base32 text into a byte array and returns the byte count, or an error.
Decodes base32 text straight to a string; the decoded bytes must be UTF-8.
Returns bytes or a string as hexadecimal text, two digits a byte, lower or upper case.
Decodes hexadecimal text into a byte array and returns the byte count, or an error.
Decodes hexadecimal text straight to a string; the decoded bytes must be UTF-8.
Returns text with the characters a URL cannot hold written as %XX escapes.
Turns %XX escapes, and + in query mode, back into text, or returns an error.
Holds why decoding failed: a code, the position of the first bad character, a message.
Reads a fixed-width integer or float at a byte offset, little- or big-endian.
Reads an unsigned variable-length integer at an offset and moves the offset past it.
Reads a signed variable-length integer at an offset and moves the offset past it.
Writes a fixed-width number at a byte offset, growing the array if it is too short.
Adds a fixed-width number to the end of a byte array, little- or big-endian.
Adds an unsigned integer to a byte array in as few bytes as it needs.
Adds a signed integer to a byte array, keeping small negative numbers short.
Holds a 128-bit identifier that can be compared, sorted and used as a Map key.
Returns a new random UUID from the system's secure random generator.
Returns a new UUID that starts with the time, so each one sorts after the one before.
Returns the nil UUID, with all 16 bytes zero.
Returns the max UUID, with every bit set.
Parses a UUID with or without hyphens, braces or a urn:uuid: prefix, or returns an error.
Returns the UUID as 36 characters of lower-case text in the 8-4-4-4-12 form.
Returns a UUID from an array of exactly 16 bytes, or an error.
Returns the UUID's 16 bytes as an Array.
Holds why a UUID did not parse: a code and the position of the offending character.
Returns the UUID's version, such as 4 or 7, or 0 for the nil UUID.
Returns the UUID's variant field, which is 1 for every standard UUID.
Returns true if all 16 bytes of the UUID are zero.
Returns when a version 7 UUID was made, in Unix milliseconds, or -1 for any other.
Returns a hash of the UUID, used when it is a Map or Set key.
Returns the digest of text or a byte array as bytes, for the algorithm named.
Returns the digest of text or a byte array as lower-case hex.
Returns the digest of a whole file, read in 64 KB pieces, or why it could not be read.
Feeds a stream from where it is to its end into a hasher; returns the bytes read.
Names the algorithms the one-call functions take, from HASH_CRC32 to HASH_SHA512.
Returns a new hasher for an algorithm, which the caller deletes, or nullptr.
Holds a CRC-32 checksum, the 4-byte one zip, gzip and PNG use.
Holds a CRC-32C checksum, the 4-byte one iSCSI and ext4 use.
Holds an Adler-32 checksum, the 4-byte one zlib streams use.
Holds a 32-bit FNV-1a hash, quick for short keys; not for security.
Holds a 64-bit FNV-1a hash, quick for short keys; not for security.
Holds a 64-bit xxHash with an optional seed, fast on large data; not for security.
Holds a 16-byte MD5 hash, only for matching formats that already use it.
Holds a 20-byte SHA-1 hash, only for matching formats that already use it.
Holds a 28-byte SHA-224 hash, for data someone could tamper with.
Holds a 32-byte SHA-256 hash, for data someone could tamper with.
Holds a 48-byte SHA-384 hash, faster than SHA-256 on long messages on 64-bit machines.
Holds a 64-byte SHA-512 hash, faster than SHA-256 on long messages on 64-bit machines.
Holds what every hash type shares, so one procedure can take any of them.
Adds a number of bytes at a pointer to the hash.
Adds the bytes of an Array to the hash.
Adds text to the hash as its UTF-8 bytes.
Adds the bytes of a string to the hash as they are, with no conversion.
Returns the digest so far as bytes; more data can still be added after it.
Returns the digest so far as lower-case hex; more data can still be added after it.
Forgets everything added and starts the hash again.
Returns the size of the digest in bytes.
Returns the size of the block the algorithm works on, in bytes.
Returns a checksum or fast hash as a number instead of bytes.
Holds an HMAC: a cryptographic hash with a key, which is itself a Hasher.
Returns the HMAC of a message under a key as lower-case hex, in one call.
Returns true if two byte arrays match, taking the same time whichever byte differs.
